name: crimson-crab

hlido_opinion.headline: A Rust Claude SDK built on one compile-time guarantee — no unwrap, expect, panic! or todo! anywhere in the library — with unknown API surface deserialising into catch-alls instead of breaking builds.
hlido_opinion.body: crimson-crab makes an unusually specific and checkable promise for an SDK: panicking macros are denied at compile time across the whole library, so a malformed or surprising API response reaches the caller as an `Error` rather than taking down a service. That is a lint-enforceable property rather than a claim about care, which is what makes it worth something. The second design decision is forward compatibility — unknown block types, stream events and stop reasons deserialise into `Unknown` catch-alls, so a new model or content type from Anthropic does not break a build on the day it ships. Anyone who has had a strongly-typed client break on an additive API change will recognise the value. Coverage is the complete Claude surface rather than a subset: streaming via a hand-rolled SSE parser with no eventsource dependency, tool use with raw JSON schemas, adaptive/budgeted/disabled thinking modes, prompt caching with 5m/1h TTL and cache hits readable off `Usage`, message batches with a JSONL-decoding result stream, token counting, and typed errors carrying `request_id` with jittered backoff honouring retry-after. The public API exposes `futures_core::Stream` rather than tokio types, which keeps it runtime-light and checks on wasm32. The caution is maturity and standing: v0.3.0 is early, MSRV 1.75, and this is a community SDK rather than an Anthropic-published one — the surface carries no adoption numbers, no named users and no third-party review. The slug also describes it as an 'MCP template', which the captured surface does not support: this is a Claude API client.

tier_rationale: STEADY (76) for a genuinely checkable core guarantee (panicking macros denied at compile time, so surprises surface as errors), forward-compatible catch-all deserialisation that survives additive API changes, and complete rather than partial Claude API coverage including streaming, batches, caching and token counting. Held well below VITAL by v0.3.0 maturity, no adoption or third-party validation on the surface, and unofficial status — a community SDK carries different risk from a vendor-published one.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A Rust SDK for building agents rather than an agent itself: tool definitions take raw JSON schemas, the agentic loop is driven by the caller, and any server-tool passes through ToolUnion::Raw. Relevant to agent builders on Rust; nothing here is agent-callable at runtime.

checklist.evidence: 'The Rust SDK for Claude that can't panic on you.'
